title: Multiple Linear Regression I
description: Recall deck covering least squares, model assumptions, goodness of fit, inference, and special explanatory variables from Chapter 3. This is part two of a two-part series.

cards.front: What is the coefficient of determination \(R^2\)?
cards.back: \(R^2=\dfrac{\mathrm{Regression}\ SS}{\mathrm{Total}\ SS}\), the proportion of variability explained by the regression function.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the relationship between \(R^2\) and the correlation of \(y\) with fitted values?
cards.back: \(R^2=[r(y,\widehat y)]^2\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Why can ordinary \(R^2\) be misleading for variable selection?
cards.back: It never decreases when an explanatory variable is added, even if the added variable is not useful.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the adjusted coefficient of determination?
cards.back: \(R_a^2=1-\dfrac{(\mathrm{Error}\ SS)/[n-(k+1)]}{(\mathrm{Total}\ SS)/(n-1)}=1-\dfrac{s^2}{s_y^2}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: How are \(s^2\) and \(R_a^2\) related as measures of fit?
cards.back: Better fit means smaller \(s^2\) and larger \(R_a^2\); minimizing \(s^2\) is equivalent to maximizing \(R_a^2\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What are the degrees of freedom in the multiple-regression ANOVA table?
cards.back: Regression: \(k\); Error: \(n-(k+1)\); Total: \(n-1\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the standard error of coefficient \(b_j\)?
cards.back: \(se(b_j)=s\sqrt{\text{the }(j+1)\text{st diagonal element of }(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What hypothesis is usually tested to determine whether explanatory variable \(x_j\) is important?
cards.back: \(H_0:\beta_j=0\) versus \(H_a:\beta_j\ne0\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the t-ratio for a regression coefficient when testing \(H_0:\beta_j=0\)?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: How is \(t(b_j)\) interpreted?
cards.back: It is the number of estimated standard errors that \(b_j\) is away from zero.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: For a two-sided t-test at significance level \(\alpha\), when is \(H_0:\beta_j=0\) rejected?
cards.back: Reject when \(|t(b_j)|>t_{n-(k+1),\,1-\alpha/2}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What rule of thumb is given for a variable's importance in a large sample?
cards.back: A variable is important if its t-ratio exceeds two in absolute value.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is the \((1-\alpha)\) confidence interval for \(\beta_j\)?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is an added variable plot?
cards.back: A plot of residuals from regressing \(y\) on the other explanatory variables against residuals from regressing \(x_j\) on those same other variables.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: How is the added variable plot for PRICE versus ECOST constructed in the refrigerator example?
cards.back: Regress PRICE on RSIZE, FSIZE, SHELVES, and FEATURES to obtain \(e_1\); regress ECOST on those variables to obtain \(e_2\); then plot \(e_1\) versus \(e_2\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What does a partial correlation coefficient measure?
cards.back: The correlation between \(y\) and \(x_j\) in the presence of the other explanatory variables.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: How can a partial correlation coefficient be calculated from a t-ratio?
cards.back: \(r(y,x_j\mid\text{others})=\dfrac{t(b_j)}{\sqrt{t(b_j)^2+n-(k+1)}}\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Why might an added variable plot be preferable to a partial correlation coefficient alone?
cards.back: The plot can reveal nonlinear relationships that a correlation coefficient may miss.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What are omitted variables, and why can they be problematic?
cards.back: They are variables left out of a regression; omission can make coefficients strongly significant when they should not be or even give them the incorrect sign.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is a binary explanatory variable also called?
cards.back: An indicator variable or dummy variable.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: In the model \(LNFACE=\beta_0+\beta_1LNINCOME+\beta_2SINGLE+\varepsilon\), how is \(\beta_2\) interpreted?
cards.back: It is the expected change in LNFACE when moving from SINGLE \(=0\) to SINGLE \(=1\), holding LNINCOME fixed.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Why can linear regression represent nonlinear functions of explanatory variables?
cards.back: The regression function must be linear in parameters, but explanatory variables can be transformed nonlinear functions such as \(x^2\), \(\ln x\), or products.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is polynomial regression as a special case of linear regression?
cards.back: Use \(x_1=x,x_2=x^2,\ldots,x_p=x^p\) in \(\mathrm{E}\,y=\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\cdots+\beta_px_p\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is an interaction term?
cards.back: A variable created as a nonlinear function of two or more explanatory variables, commonly \(x_3=x_1x_2\).
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: In \(\mathrm{E}\,y=\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2+\beta_3x_1x_2\), what is \(\partial\mathrm{E}\,y/\partial x_1\)?
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: Why cannot \(x_3=x_1+x_2\) be used as an estimable interaction-like explanatory variable alongside \(x_1\) and \(x_2\)?
cards.back: It is a linear combination of existing explanatory variables, so all parameters cannot be estimated.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex

cards.front: What is piecewise linear regression?
cards.back: A model with linear relationships in regions separated by one or more kinks, often using binary variables to join the pieces.
source_ids: Regression Modeling with Actuarial and Financial Applications_014 - 3 Multiple Linear Regression - I.tex
